data.long_meaning: Jiyaur is a Sanskrit name derived from 'ji' (victorious) and 'yaur' (Jiva or soul). The name signifies the triumph of the soul over obstacles and challenges. It is a powerful name for a baby boy in Hindu tradition. The name Jiyaur carries the meaning “Victorious Jiva” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jiyaur usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious jiva and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Jiyaur belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victorious Jiva.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jiyaur total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Jiyaur was a Chalukya king who ruled the Eastern Chalukya Empire in the 11th century. He is known for his military conquests and the construction of the temple at Puliyangudi.
historical_references.context: The Eastern Chalukya Empire was a branch of the Chalukya dynasty which ruled large parts of the Deccan plateau in present-day India. Jiyaur succeeded his father Bhima I and was followed by his son Vijayaditya.

historical_references.reference: Jiyaur was also a military commander in the armies of the Chalukya king, Satyashraya, in the late 10th century. He is known for his victories against the Chola dynasty and the Western Chalukyas.
historical_references.context: During the reign of Satyashraya, the Chalukyas faced threats from both the Cholas in the south and the Western Chalukyas in the west. Jiyaur played a significant role in repelling these invaders and expanding the Chalukya Empire.
